    def project_write_image_code(args: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        image = str(args.get("image") or args.get("path") or "").strip()
        rel = str(args.get("rel_path") or args.get("rel") or "").strip()
        if not image:
            return err_result("project.write_image_code", "image required")
        if not Path(image).is_file():
            return err_result("project.write_image_code", "image file required")
        if not rel:
            return err_result("project.write_image_code", "rel_path required")
        snap = _call_on_ui(window, lambda: _vision_snap(window))
        if not isinstance(snap, dict) or not str(snap.get("model") or "").strip():
            return err_result("project.write_image_code", "model required")
        raw = extract_image_code(
            image,
            model=str(snap["model"]),
            ollama_base_url=str(snap.get("ollama_base_url") or ""),
            api_base_url=str(snap.get("api_base_url") or ""),
            api_key=str(snap.get("api_key") or ""),
            auth_style=str(snap.get("auth_style") or "bearer"),
        )
        code = extracted_code(raw)
        if not code:
            return err_result("project.write_image_code", "extraction had no code")
        root = str(args.get("project_root") or snap.get("project_root") or "").strip()
        payload = {
            "project_root": root,
            "rel_path": rel,
            "content": code,
            "open": True,
        }
        written = _write_on_ui(window, payload)
        if not isinstance(written, dict):
            return err_result("project.write_image_code", "write timed out")
        if not written.get("ok"):
            return err_result(
                "project.write_image_code",
                str(written.get("error") or "write failed"),
                written.get("result") if isinstance(written.get("result"), dict) else {},
            )
        out = dict(written)
        out["action"] = "project.write_image_code"
        return out

        risk="medium",

    """?먯떇 ?꾨줈?몄뒪 ?꾩슜. ?몄텧痢?IRIS ?꾨줈?몄뒪?먯꽌 吏곸젒 遺瑜댁? 留?寃?"""

            detail = (proc.stderr or proc.stdout or "PDF ?앹꽦???ㅽ뙣?덉뒿?덈떎.").strip()
        fail = _failure(detail.splitlines()[-1][:300] if detail else "PDF ?앹꽦???ㅽ뙣?덉뒿?덈떎.")
        trace(f"[PDF] generation failed: {fail['error']}")
        return fail
    trace("[PDF] generation completed")
    return {"ok": True, "path": str(dest.resolve()), "error": ""}


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Write a text PDF (child process).")
    parser.add_argument("--text", default="")
    parser.add_argument("--out", default="")
    parser.add_argument("--abort", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.abort:
        os.abort()
    if not args.text or not args.out:
        print("text and out required", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    try:
        body = Path(args.text).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        write_pdf_file(body, Path(args.out))
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 ???먯떇? 硫붿떆吏留??④린怨?二쎈뒗??
        print(str(exc), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

from iris.ui.chat.file_write_claim import CHAT_ONLY
from iris.ui.window import main_window as mw


def _ev(**kwargs) -> TurnEvidence:
    base = dict(
        tool_ok_count=0,
        tool_written=False,
        verified_path="",
        content_match=None,
        empty_reply=False,
        assistant="",
        goal="",
    )
    base.update(kwargs)
    return TurnEvidence(**base)


def _check() -> None:
    soft = verify_file_create_turn(
        _ev(
            assistant="肄붾뱶???묒꽦???꾨즺?덉뒿?덈떎. ?뚯씪 ?대쫫? tetris_king.py ?낅땲??",
            goal="?뚰듃由ъ뒪??肄붾뱶 ?묒꽦?댁쨾",
        )
    )
    assert CHAT_ONLY in soft.display
    assert FILE_CREATE_EXPLICIT_FAIL in soft.display
    assert "display" in soft.actions
    assert "stop" in soft.actions
    assert "failover" not in soft.actions
    assert soft.suppress_voice_followup
    assert soft.suppress_followthrough

    soft_failover = verify_file_create_turn(
        _ev(
            assistant="肄붾뱶???묒꽦???꾨즺?덉뒿?덈떎. ?뚯씪 ?대쫫? tetris_king.py ?낅땲??",
            goal="?뚰듃由ъ뒪??肄붾뱶 ?묒꽦?댁쨾",
        ),
        failover_available=True,
    )
    assert CHAT_ONLY in soft_failover.display
    assert FILE_CREATE_EXPLICIT_FAIL not in soft_failover.display
    assert "failover" in soft_failover.actions
    assert "stop" not in soft_failover.actions
    assert soft_failover.suppress_followthrough

    empty_fail = verify_file_create_turn(
        _ev(
            empty_reply=True,
            assistant="",
            goal="?뚰듃由ъ뒪 肄붾뱶 ?묒꽦?댁쨾",
        )
    )
    assert empty_fail.display == FILE_CREATE_EXPLICIT_FAIL
    assert "stop" in empty_fail.actions
    assert empty_fail.suppress_followthrough

    empty_failover = verify_file_create_turn(
        _ev(
            empty_reply=True,
            assistant="",
            goal="?뚰듃由ъ뒪 肄붾뱶 ?묒꽦?댁쨾",
        ),
        failover_available=True,
    )
    assert "failover" in empty_failover.actions
    assert empty_failover.suppress_followthrough
    assert not (empty_failover.display or "").strip()

    planned = verify_file_create_turn(
        _ev(
            assistant="tetris_king.py\n```python\nprint(1)\n```",
            goal="?뚰듃由ъ뒪??肄붾뱶 ?묒꽦???ㅼ쓬???ㅽ뻾?댁쨾",
        )
    )
    assert "local_write" in planned.actions
    assert "failover" not in planned.actions
    assert "stop" not in planned.actions
    assert not planned.suppress_followthrough
    assert planned.local_plan is not None
    assert planned.local_plan.kind == "write"
    assert planned.local_plan.pairs[0][0] == "tetris_king.py"

    evidenced = verify_file_create_turn(
        _ev(
            tool_ok_count=1,
            tool_written=True,
            assistant="肄붾뱶???묒꽦???꾨즺?덉뒿?덈떎.",
            goal="?ㅽ겕由쏀듃 留뚮뱾?댁쨾",
        )
    )
    assert CHAT_ONLY not in evidenced.display
    assert "local_write" not in evidenced.actions
    assert "failover" not in evidenced.actions
    assert not evidenced.suppress_followthrough

    mismatch = verify_file_create_turn(
        _ev(
            tool_ok_count=1,
            tool_written=True,
            content_match=False,
            assistant="肄붾뱶???묒꽦???꾨즺?덉뒿?덈떎.",
            goal="?ㅽ겕由쏀듃 留뚮뱾?댁쨾",
        )
    )
    assert CHAT_ONLY in mismatch.display
    assert "local_write" in mismatch.actions or "ask" in mismatch.actions or "display" in mismatch.actions

    weather = verify_file_create_turn(
        _ev(
            empty_reply=True,
            assistant="",
            goal="?ㅻ뒛 ?좎뵪 ?뚮젮以?,
        )
    )
    assert "failover" not in weather.actions
    assert "stop" not in weather.actions
    assert not weather.suppress_followthrough

    src = inspect.getsource(mw.MainWindow._on_chat_finished)
    assert "_run_file_create_verify_turn" in src
    assert "_fire_file_create_failover" in src or "failover" in src
    assert "_file_create_failover_available" in inspect.getsource(mw.MainWindow)
    print("turn_verify ok")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _check()

def _internal() -> InternalSidecar:
    return InternalSidecar(home=EngineHome(Path.home() / ".iris-light" / "engine"))


class _StubEngine:
    def __init__(self, *, ready=None, events=None) -> None:
        self.source = _internal()
        self.ready = ready or EngineReady(self.source, "engine is ready")
        self.events = list(events or [])
        self.turns: list[object] = []
        self.ensure_calls = 0

    def ensure_ready(self):
        self.ensure_calls += 1
        return self.ready

    def run_turn(self, turn):
        self.turns.append(turn)
        yield from self.events


class _Collector:
    def __init__(self, worker) -> None:
        self.ok: list[object] = []
        self.failed: list[str] = []
        self.notice: list[str] = []
        self.content: list[str] = []
        self.tools: list[str] = []
        worker.finished_ok.connect(self.ok.append)
        worker.failed.connect(self.failed.append)
        if hasattr(worker, "notice"):
            worker.notice.connect(self.notice.append)
        if hasattr(worker, "content_chunk"):
            worker.content_chunk.connect(self.content.append)
        if hasattr(worker, "tool_progress"):
            worker.tool_progress.connect(self.tools.append)

def _turn(*, cancelled: bool = False) -> StatelessTurn:
    token = CancelToken()
    if cancelled:
        token.cancel()
    return StatelessTurn(
        transcript=ChatTranscript.parse([{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]),
        model=HermesInferenceTarget(model="llama3.2", provider="custom"),
        cancel=token,

        self.assertIn("Engine", engine.__all__)

        self.assertEqual(len(events), 1)

    def test_cancelled_turn_yields_turn_cancelled(self) -> None:
        engine = Engine(self._internal())

    def test_mid_turn_cancel_kills_child_and_yields_cancelled(self) -> None:
        from unittest.mock import MagicMock

        engine = Engine(self._internal())
        fake = MagicMock()
        fake.poll.return_value = None
        engine._child = fake
        token = CancelToken()
        turn = StatelessTurn(
            transcript=ChatTranscript.parse([{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]),
            model=HermesInferenceTarget(model="llama3.2", provider="custom"),
            cancel=token,
        )

        def read(*_a, **_k):
            token.cancel()
            return ""

        order: list[str] = []

        def on_stop(*_a, **_k):
            order.append("stop")

        def on_forget(*_a, **_k):
            order.append("forget")

        with (
            patch.object(
                engine,
                "ensure_ready",
                return_value=EngineReady(self._internal(), "ready"),
            ),
            patch.object(engine, "_write_turn"),
            patch("iris.engine.runtime._readline_timeout", side_effect=read),
            patch("iris.engine.runtime._send_stop", side_effect=on_stop),
            patch.object(engine, "_forget_child", side_effect=on_forget),
        ):
            events = list(engine.run_turn(turn))
        self.assertEqual(events, [TurnCancelled()])
        self.assertEqual(order, ["stop", "forget"])

    def test_ollama_turn_sends_compat_api_key(self) -> None:
        turn = StatelessTurn(

                provider="custom",
                base_url="http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1",
            ),
            cancel=CancelToken(),
        )
        self.assertEqual(_turn_api_key(turn), "ollama")
        keyed = StatelessTurn(
            transcript=turn.transcript,
            model=HermesInferenceTarget(
                model="gpt",
                provider="custom",
                base_url="https://api.example/v1",
                api_key="sk-user",
            ),
            cancel=CancelToken(),
        )
        self.assertEqual(_turn_api_key(keyed), "sk-user")

def _call_on_ui(window: MainWindow, fn: Callable[[], Any]) -> Any:
    """UI ?꾩젽 ?묎렐 留덉꺃. ?대? 硫붿씤?대㈃ 吏곸젒 ?몄텧 (Queued+wait ?곕뱶??湲덉?)."""
    try:
        from PyQt6.QtCore import QThread

        if QThread.currentThread() is window.thread():
            return fn()
    except Exception:
        return fn()
    qt = getattr(window, "_control_qt_invoker", None)
    if qt is None:
        return fn()
    try:
        return qt.run(fn, timeout=3.0)
    except Exception:
        return None


def _call_on_ui_unbounded(window: MainWindow, fn: Callable[[], Any]) -> Any:
    """HUD confirm waits until the dialog returns. The 3s UI marshal is too short."""
    try:
        from PyQt6.QtCore import QThread

        if QThread.currentThread() is window.thread():
            return fn()
    except Exception:
        return fn()
    qt = getattr(window, "_control_qt_invoker", None)
    if qt is None:
        return fn()
    return qt.run(fn, timeout=None)

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from iris.knowledge.wiki_places import is_sensitive

_MAX_FILES = 8
_MAX_CHARS = 200_000


def resolve_pdf_dest(raw: str, project_root: str = "") -> Path:
    """?곷? 寃쎈줈???대┛ ?꾨줈?앺듃. 鍮꾩슦硫??꾨줈?앺듃 ?먮뒗 Documents/IRIS."""
    text = (raw or "").strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    root = Path(project_root).expanduser() if (project_root or "").strip() else None
    if text:
        dest = Path(text).expanduser()
        if not dest.is_absolute() and root is not None:
            dest = root / dest
        if dest.suffix.lower() != ".pdf":
            dest = dest.with_suffix(".pdf")
        return dest
    if root is not None and root.is_dir():
        return root / "iris-note.pdf"
    return Path.home() / "Documents" / "IRIS" / "iris-note.pdf"


def compose_pdf_text(content: str, sources: list[str], project_root: str = "") -> str:
    """content? ?뚯씪 蹂몃Ц????PDF 臾몄옄?대줈. 鍮꾨? ?뺥깭 以꾩? 吏?대떎."""
    parts: list[str] = []
    body = _redact(content or "").strip()
    if body:
        parts.append(body)
    root = Path(project_root).expanduser().resolve() if (project_root or "").strip() else None
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for raw in sources[:_MAX_FILES]:
        path = _source_path(str(raw or ""), root)
        if path is None:
            continue
        key = str(path).casefold()
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        try:
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        except OSError:
            continue
        text = _redact(text)[:_MAX_CHARS].strip()
        if not text:
            continue
        parts.append(f"# {path.name}\n\n{text}")
    return "\n\n".join(parts).strip()


def source_list(args: dict) -> list[str]:
    raw = args.get("sources")
    if raw is None:
        raw = args.get("files")
    if isinstance(raw, str):
        items = [raw]
    elif isinstance(raw, list):
        items = [str(item) for item in raw]
    else:
        items = []
    one = str(args.get("source") or args.get("file") or "").strip()
    if one:
        items.append(one)
    return [item.strip() for item in items if str(item).strip()]


def _source_path(raw: str, root: Path | None) -> Path | None:
    text = raw.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    if not text or "\x00" in text:
        return None
    path = Path(text).expanduser()
    if not path.is_absolute() and root is not None:
        path = root / path
    try:
        path = path.resolve()
    except OSError:
        return None
    if not path.is_file():
        return None
    if root is not None and root.is_dir() and path != root and root not in path.parents:
        if Path(text).expanduser().is_absolute():
            return path
        return None
    return path


def _redact(text: str) -> str:
    kept: list[str] = []
    for line in (text or "").splitlines():
        kept.append("[redacted]" if is_sensitive(line) else line)
    return "\n".join(kept)

def _on_tool(kind: object = None, *args: object, **kwargs: object) -> None:
    if kind is None and args:
        kind = args[0]
        args = args[1:]
    if kind is None:
        kind = kwargs.get("label", "")
    name = args[0] if args else kwargs.get("name")
    label = tool_use_label(kind, name)
    if label:
        _emit({"t": "tool", "label": label})
    _emit_app_ui_from_tool(kind, name, args, kwargs)
    if label:
        return
    kind_text = "" if kind is None else str(kind)
    if kind_text == "reasoning.available":
        _emit_reasoning_fallback(args, kwargs)
        return
    if kind_text in _NOT_A_TOOL_NAME:
        return
    if kind_text:
        _emit({"t": "tool", "label": kind_text})


def _on_reasoning(text: object) -> None:
    global _reasoning_streamed
    if text is None:
        return
    chunk = str(text)
    if not chunk:
        return
    _reasoning_streamed = True
    _emit({"t": "think", "text": chunk})


def _emit_reasoning_fallback(args: tuple[object, ...], kwargs: dict[str, object]) -> None:
    if _reasoning_streamed:
        return
    preview = args[1] if len(args) > 1 else kwargs.get("preview")
    if preview is None:
        return
    chunk = str(preview)
    if chunk:
        _emit({"t": "think", "text": chunk})


def _done_text(result: object) -> str:
    if isinstance(result, dict):
        return str(result.get("final_response") or "")
    if result is None:
        return ""
    return str(result)

_TURN_ENDED_LOG_POLL_SEC = 0.25

def _run_agent_turn(cls: type, history: list, user: str, raw: dict) -> None:
    global _reasoning_streamed
    _reasoning_streamed = False
    streamed_parts: list[str] = []
    returned = threading.Event()
    release = threading.Event()
    terminal = threading.Event()
    terminal_lock = threading.Lock()
    armed = threading.Event()
    stop_poll = threading.Event()
    outcome: dict[str, object] = {}

    def on_delta(text: object) -> None:
        if text is None:
            return
        chunk = str(text)
        if not chunk:
            return
        streamed_parts.append(chunk)
        _emit({"t": "delta", "text": chunk})

    def on_turn_ended() -> None:
        # Handler + file poll share one arm. Prefer landing immediately when
        # stream already has text. If not, wait briefly for return.
        if armed.is_set():
            return
        armed.set()
        try:

            if text:

                        terminal, terminal_lock, text=text
                    ):

                        release.set()
                        return
                    time.sleep(0.05 * (attempt + 1))
                # Leave terminal clear so the worker-return path retries emit.
                stop_poll.set()
                return

            stop_poll.set()

            def _watch() -> None:
                if returned.wait(_POST_TURN_END_GRACE_SEC):
                    return
                late = "".join(streamed_parts).strip() or _assistant_text_from_agent(
                    agent

def _watch_trace(msg: str) -> None:
    # Critical landing lines stay synchronous so measure can see them before exit.
    # Non-critical miss spam stays fire-and-forget to avoid log-lock freezes.
    line = f"pid={os.getpid()} host {msg}\n"
    critical = msg.startswith(("recv ", "read_turn_events", "run_turn started"))
    if not critical:

        def _write() -> None:
            try:
                _WATCH_LOG.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                with _WATCH_LOG.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                    fh.write(line)
            except Exception:
                return

        threading.Thread(target=_write, name="iris-host-watch", daemon=True).start()
        return
    try:
        _WATCH_LOG.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with _WATCH_LOG.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:

    except Exception:

def _terminal_dir() -> Path:
    env = os.environ.get("IRIS_TERMINAL_DIR", "").strip()
    if env:
        return Path(env)
    # TEMP avoids AV/exclusive locks under ~/.iris-light/logs that wedge is_file().
    return Path(os.environ.get("TEMP") or os.environ.get("TMP") or ".") / (
        "iris-sidecar-terminal"
    )


def _read_terminal_file_impl(hello_pid: int | None) -> str:
    """Sidecar writes done/fail here when the stdout pipe EINVAL.

    Open-try only ??Path.is_file()/stat can block under Windows Defender while
    the sidecar creates the file, and a timed wrapper that abandons the reader
    then unlinks the only land path.
    """
    if hello_pid is None or hello_pid <= 0:
        return ""
    path = _terminal_dir() / f"{int(hello_pid)}.ndjson"
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            text = fh.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return ""
    except OSError:
        return ""
    if not text.strip():
        return ""
    try:
        path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    except OSError:
        pass
    _watch_trace(
        f"recv terminal_file hello_pid={hello_pid} path={path.name} "
        f"chars={len(text.strip())}"
    )
    return text if text.endswith("\n") else text + "\n"


def _read_terminal_file(hello_pid: int | None, *, timeout: float = 0.25) -> str:
    """UI/timer helper. Prefer impl directly ??do not abandon a reader mid-unlink."""
    del timeout  # kept for call-site compat; abandoned timed reads lose the file
    try:
        return _read_terminal_file_impl(hello_pid)
    except Exception:
        return ""

def _sidecar_env(home: EngineHome, python: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    env = _stripped_probe_env(home=home, python=python)
    for key in _GATEWAY_ENV_KEYS:
        env.pop(key, None)
    env["HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS"] = "1"
    env["IRIS_ENGINE_GUI_PYTHON"] = sys.executable
    # Unique per spawn so turn-end file poll cannot steal another sidecar's line.
    log_path = Path(home) / "logs" / f"sidecar-{time.time_ns()}.log"
    log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    env["IRIS_ENGINE_LOG"] = str(log_path)
    env["PYTHONUNBUFFERED"] = "1"
    # Korean Windows defaults to cp949 for child stdio; parent pipes are utf-8.
    env["PYTHONUTF8"] = "1"
    env["PYTHONIOENCODING"] = "utf-8"
    terminal_dir = Path(os.environ.get("TEMP") or os.environ.get("TMP") or ".") / (
        "iris-sidecar-terminal"
    )
    terminal_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    env["IRIS_TERMINAL_DIR"] = str(terminal_dir)
    os.environ["IRIS_TERMINAL_DIR"] = str(terminal_dir)
    return env


def _bind_terminal_udp() -> tuple[socket.socket, int]:
    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    sock.settimeout(0.5)
    port = int(sock.getsockname()[1])
    return sock, port


def _hello_ok(line: str) -> bool:
    try:
        raw = json.loads(line)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return False
    if not (isinstance(raw, dict) and raw.get("t") == "hello" and bool(raw.get("ok"))):
        return False
    child_pid = raw.get("pid")
    _watch_trace(f"sidecar hello ok child_pid={child_pid}")
    return True


def _hello_pid(line: str) -> int | None:
    try:
        raw = json.loads(line)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return None
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        return None
    try:
        pid = int(raw.get("pid") or 0)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    return pid if pid > 0 else None


def _readline_timeout(
    stream: object,
    timeout: float,
    cancel: CancelToken | None = None,
) -> str:
    if stream is None:
        return ""
    box: list[str] = []

    def _read() -> None:
        try:
            box.append(stream.readline())  # type: ignore[union-attr]
        except Exception:
            box.append("")

    worker = threading.Thread(target=_read, daemon=True)
    worker.start()
    deadline = time.monotonic() + max(0.0, timeout)
    cancelled = False
    while worker.is_alive():
        remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
        if remaining <= 0:
            break
        if cancel is not None and cancel.cancelled():
            cancelled = True
            break
        worker.join(min(_CANCEL_POLL_SEC, remaining))
    if cancelled:
        # Do not abandon a live readline on this stream; caller kills the child
        # next, which unblocks the reader. Join so a later turn cannot race.
        worker.join(2.0)
        return ""
    if worker.is_alive():
        return ""
    if not box:
        return ""
    return box[0]


def _close_pipes(proc: subprocess.Popen[str]) -> None:
    for stream in (proc.stdin, proc.stdout, proc.stderr):
        if stream is None:
            continue
        try:
            stream.close()
        except OSError:
            continue

def _turn_api_key(turn: StatelessTurn) -> str:
    """Hermes `_init_openai_client` only takes the explicit path when both
    api_key and base_url are set. Ollama's OpenAI adapter accepts any token."""

def _spawn_sidecar(
    home: EngineHome,
) -> EngineFailed | tuple[subprocess.Popen[str], int | None]:
    python = engine_python(home)
    if python is None:
        return _failed(EngineErrorCode.NOT_INSTALLED, "engine python is not installed")
    python_path = Path(python)
    try:
        proc = subprocess.Popen(
            [str(python_path), str(_SIDECAR_MAIN)],
            stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            text=True,
            encoding="utf-8",
            errors="replace",
            env=_sidecar_env(home, python_path),
            cwd=str(home),
            **no_window_kwargs(),
        )
    except OSError as exc:
        return _failed(EngineErrorCode.SPAWN_FAILED, f"sidecar spawn failed: {exc}")
    line = _readline_timeout(proc.stdout, _HELLO_TIMEOUT_SEC)
    if _hello_ok(line):

    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        pass

    if code == 2:
        return _failed(EngineErrorCode.WRONG_PYTHON, "sidecar refused this interpreter")
    if not line.strip():
        return _failed(EngineErrorCode.SPAWN_FAILED, "sidecar hello timed out or was empty")
    return _failed(EngineErrorCode.SPAWN_FAILED, f"sidecar hello was not valid: {line.strip()[:200]}")


class Engine:
    """One sidecar, one lock, one home."""

    def __init__(self, source: EngineSource) -> None:
        self._source = source
        self._lock = Lock()
        self._child: subprocess.Popen[str] | None = None
        self._child_hello_pid: int | None = None
        # True while a turn owns the child for I/O outside _lock. Shutdown ignores it.
        self._turn_active = False
        self._tool_handler: Callable[[str, dict[str, object]], dict[str, object]] | None = None

    @property
    def source(self) -> EngineSource:
        """Parsed source for this handle. Same object shared_engine() stored."""
        return self._source

    def fork(self) -> Engine:
        """Return an independent sidecar owner for one concurrent chat worker."""
        return Engine(self._source)

    def bind_tool_handler(
        self, handler: Callable[[str, dict[str, object]], dict[str, object]]
    ) -> None:
        self._tool_handler = handler

    def ensure_ready(self) -> EngineEnsureResult:
        try:
            with self._lock:
                if self._child is not None:
                    if self._child.poll() is None:
                        return EngineReady(self._source, "engine is ready")
                    _close_pipes(self._child)
                    self._child = None
                    self._child_hello_pid = None
                if isinstance(self._source, ExternalGateway):
                    return EngineFailed(
                        EngineError(
                            EngineErrorCode.UNKNOWN,
                            "external Hermes gateway is not wired",
                        )
                    )
                if isinstance(self._source, InternalSidecar):
                    home = self._source.home
                    probe = probe_engine_python(home)
                    if probe is not None and (
                        probe.code == EngineErrorCode.NOT_INSTALLED
                        or engine_python(home) is None
                    ):
                        install_into(home)
                        probe = probe_engine_python(home)
                    if probe is not None:
                        return EngineFailed(probe)
                    spawned = _spawn_sidecar(home)
                    if isinstance(spawned, EngineFailed):
                        return spawned
                    self._child, self._child_hello_pid = spawned
                    return EngineReady(self._source, "engine is ready")
                return EngineFailed(
                    EngineError(
                        EngineErrorCode.NOT_INSTALLED,
                        "engine sidecar is not installed",
                    )
                )
        except Exception as exc:
            return EngineFailed(EngineError(EngineErrorCode.UNKNOWN, str(exc)))

    def _forget_child(self) -> None:
        child = self._child
        self._child = None
        self._child_hello_pid = None
        if child is None:
            return
        if child.poll() is None:
            _terminate_child(child)
            return
        _close_pipes(child)

    def _stop_and_forget(self) -> None:
        # Cooperative stdin stop first; _forget_child still taskkills if the turn is stuck.
        # Takes _lock so shutdown can run while another thread is mid-read.
        with self._lock:
            child = self._child
            hello_pid = self._child_hello_pid
            if child is not None:
                _send_stop(child)
            self._forget_child()
        # Popen.pid may be a venv stub; also kill the hello pid that runs _sidecar_main.
        for pid in (hello_pid,):
            if pid is None:
                continue
            try:
                import psutil

                if psutil.pid_exists(int(pid)):
                    psutil.Process(int(pid)).kill()
                    _watch_trace(f"stop killed hello_pid={pid}")
            except Exception:
                pass

    def _forget_if_current(self, child: subprocess.Popen[str]) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            if self._child is child:
                self._forget_child()

    def _write_turn(
        self,
        child: subprocess.Popen[str],
        turn: StatelessTurn,
        *,
        terminal_udp_port: int | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if child.stdin is None:
            raise OSError("sidecar stdin is missing")
        fields: dict[str, object] = {
            "messages": [
                {"role": message.role.value, "content": message.content}
                for message in turn.transcript.messages
            ],
            "model": turn.model.model,
            "provider": turn.model.provider,
        }
        if turn.model.base_url:
            fields["base_url"] = turn.model.base_url
        api_key = _turn_api_key(turn)
        if api_key:
            fields["api_key"] = api_key
        if terminal_udp_port is not None:
            fields["terminal_udp_port"] = int(terminal_udp_port)
        child.stdin.write(encode_host_command("turn", **fields))
        child.stdin.flush()

    def _reply_to_tool_request(
        self, child: subprocess.Popen[str], raw: dict[str, object]
    ) -> None:
        request_id = str(raw.get("id") or "").strip()
        name = str(raw.get("name") or "").strip()
        args = raw.get("args")
        if not isinstance(args, dict):
            args = {}

            result: dict[str, object] = {
                "ok": False,
                "error": "invalid native tool request",

        elif self._tool_handler is None:
            result = {"ok": False, "error": "native tool bridge is not bound"}
        else:
            try:

class HermesHealthWorker(QThread):
    """Engine ready check. ExternalGateway keeps the :8642 health path."""

    finished_ok = pyqtSignal(bool)
    failed = pyqtSignal(str)
    notice = pyqtSignal(str)

    def __init__(self, parent=None) -> None:
        super().__init__(parent)

    def run(self) -> None:
        try:
            source = _engine_source()
            if isinstance(source, ExternalGateway):
                self._run_external(source)
                return
            result = shared_engine().ensure_ready()
            if isinstance(result, EngineFailed):
                self.failed.emit(result.user_message)
                return
            if isinstance(result, EngineReady) and result.summary:
                self.notice.emit(result.summary)
            if isinstance(source, InternalSidecar):
                try:
                    report = sync_iris_control(
                        home=source.home,
                        reconnect_gateway=False,
                    )
                    self.notice.emit(report.summary_line())
                except Exception as sync_exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                    self.notice.emit(
                        f"Iris↔engine control sync skip: {str(sync_exc)[:120]}"
                    )
            self.finished_ok.emit(True)
        except Exception as e:
            self.failed.emit(str(e))

    def _run_external(self, source: ExternalGateway) -> None:
        base_url = source.base_url
        api_key = source.api_key
        command = "hermes"
        ensure_hermes_provider_config()
        try:
            report = sync_iris_control(reconnect_gateway=True)
            self.notice.emit(report.summary_line())
            for msg in report.messages[:6]:
                if msg and msg not in report.summary_line():
                    self.notice.emit(msg)
            if report.mcp_fail_count:
                self.notice.emit(
                    f"MCP 점검 실패 {report.mcp_fail_count}개 — 설정·경로를 확인하세요."
                )

            if report.needs_gateway_reload:
                self.notice.emit("MCP 연결 — Iris Agent gateway 완전 재기동…")
                ok = restart_hermes_gateway(
                    base_url,
                    api_key=api_key,
                    command=command,
                    wait_sec=60.0,
                )
                if ok:
                    mcp_ok, mcp_detail = verify_iris_mcp_tools(command=command)
                    if mcp_ok:
                        self.notice.emit(f"Iris Agent MCP 재연결 완료 — {mcp_detail}")
                    else:
                        self.notice.emit(
                            f"Gateway는 떴지만 MCP 검증 실패: {mcp_detail}"
                        )
                        ok = False
                else:
                    from iris.system.hermes_gateway import (
                        get_last_gateway_diagnosis,
                        hermes_runtime_report,
                    )

                    report = hermes_runtime_report(command=command)
                    diag = get_last_gateway_diagnosis()
                    why = diag.user_message() if diag is not None else report
                    self.notice.emit(why[:800])
                self.finished_ok.emit(ok)
                return

            gateway_up = is_hermes_gateway_running(base_url, api_key=api_key)
            if gateway_up:
                mcp_ok, mcp_detail = verify_iris_mcp_tools(command=command)
                if mcp_ok:
                    self.notice.emit(f"MCP 유지 확인 — {mcp_detail}")
                    self.finished_ok.emit(True)
                    return
                self.notice.emit(f"MCP 미연결({mcp_detail}) — gateway 재기동…")
                ok = restart_hermes_gateway(
                    base_url,
                    api_key=api_key,
                    command=command,
                    wait_sec=60.0,
                )
                if ok:
                    mcp_ok2, mcp_detail2 = verify_iris_mcp_tools(command=command)
                    self.notice.emit(
                        f"Iris Agent MCP 재연결: {mcp_detail2}"
                        if mcp_ok2
                        else f"MCP 재검증 실패: {mcp_detail2}"
                    )
                    ok = mcp_ok2
                else:
                    from iris.system.hermes_gateway import (
                        get_last_gateway_diagnosis,
                        hermes_runtime_report,
                    )

                    report = hermes_runtime_report(command=command)
                    diag = get_last_gateway_diagnosis()
                    self.notice.emit(
                        (diag.user_message() if diag is not None else report)[:800]
                    )
                self.finished_ok.emit(ok)
                return
        except Exception as sync_exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            self.notice.emit(f"Iris Agent control sync skip: {str(sync_exc)[:120]}")

        if is_hermes_gateway_running(base_url, api_key=api_key):
            self.finished_ok.emit(True)
            return
        self.notice.emit("Iris Agent gateway가 꺼져 있습니다. 시작합니다…")
        ok = ensure_hermes_gateway_running(
            base_url,
            api_key=api_key,
            command=command,
        )
        if ok:
            mcp_ok, mcp_detail = verify_iris_mcp_tools(command=command)
            self.notice.emit(
                f"Iris Agent gateway 시작됨 — {mcp_detail}"
                if mcp_ok
                else f"Gateway 시작됐지만 MCP 실패: {mcp_detail}"
            )
            ok = mcp_ok
        else:
            from iris.system.hermes_gateway import get_last_gateway_diagnosis

            diag = get_last_gateway_diagnosis()
            if diag is not None:
                self.notice.emit(diag.user_message()[:400])
            else:
                self.notice.emit(
                    "Iris Agent gateway를 시작할 수 없습니다. "
                    "설치·포트 8642·로그(%LOCALAPPDATA%\\hermes\\logs\\iris-gateway)를 확인하세요."
                )
        self.finished_ok.emit(ok)

def shared_engine() -> Engine:
    """Process singleton. First call parses settings. Later calls return the same object."""
    global _SHARED
    with _SHARED_LOCK:
        if _SHARED is None:
            _SHARED = Engine(parse_engine_source(_settings_from_env()))
        return _SHARED


def reset_shared_engine() -> None:
    global _SHARED
    with _SHARED_LOCK:
        engine = _SHARED
        _SHARED = None
    if engine is not None:
        engine.shutdown()

        last_error = ""
        shared = shared_engine()
        fork = getattr(shared, "fork", None)
        engine = fork() if callable(fork) else shared
        bind_tools = getattr(engine, "bind_tool_handler", None)
        if callable(bind_tools):
            bind_tools(self.invoke_native_tool)
        try:
            for index, attempt in enumerate(self._attempts):
                if self._cancel_token.cancelled():
                    break
                self._final_model = attempt.model
                target = self._resolve_target(attempt)
                self.connecting.emit(target.label or attempt.label, "engine")
                content_parts: list[str] = []
                try:
                    turn = StatelessTurn(
                        transcript=ChatTranscript.parse(attempt.messages),
                        model=target,
                        cancel=self._cancel_token,
                    )
                except EngineError as exc:
                    last_error = exc.user_message or exc.detail
                    break
                finished = False
                fallback_error = last_error
                for event in engine.run_turn(turn):
                    if isinstance(event, ContentDelta):
                        if event.text:
                            content_parts.append(event.text)
                            self.content_chunk.emit(event.text)
                    elif isinstance(event, ToolProgress):
                        if event.label:
                            self.tool_progress.emit(event.label)
                    elif isinstance(event, AppUiOfferEvent):
                        if event.html_path:
                            self.app_ui.emit(event.title or "앱", event.html_path)
                    elif isinstance(event, ReasoningDelta):
                        if event.text:
                            self.reasoning.emit(event.text)
                    elif isinstance(event, TurnFinished):
                        text = "".join(content_parts) or event.text
                        _watch_trace(f"finished_ok text_len={len(text or '')}")
                        self.finished_ok.emit(text)
                        _watch_trace(f"finished_ok returned text_len={len(text or '')}")
                        finished = True
                        break
                    elif isinstance(event, TurnCancelled):
                        _watch_trace("cancelled")
                        return
                    elif isinstance(event, TurnFailed):
                        last_error = event.error.user_message or event.error.detail
                        fallback_error = event.error.detail or last_error
                        _watch_trace(f"turn_failed detail={fallback_error[:160]!r}")
                        break
                if finished:
                    return
                if self._cancel_token.cancelled():
                    break
                step = decide_fallback(fallback_error, index)
                if step is None:
                    break
                if step.cool_until_monotonic is not None:
                    self.cooled.emit(
                        route_target_for_attempt(attempt, "hermes"),
                        step.cool_until_monotonic,
                    )
                if index + 1 >= len(self._attempts):
                    break
                self._sleep_ms(step.delay_ms)
                if self._cancel_token.cancelled():

                self.switched.emit(

                self.failed.emit(last_error or "모델 응답 실패")
        finally:
            if engine is not shared:
                engine.shutdown()

class ExecKind(str, Enum):

    PURE = "pure"
    SURFACE = "surface"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SpeakGrant:
    """One agent-callable Control action. Name == ActionRegistry action id."""

    action: str
    kind: ExecKind
    summary: str = ""
    parameters: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SpeakToolRow:

    summary: str

    confirm_required: bool
    risk: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ToolResult:
    """Domain result. Not HTTP/MCP wire."""

    ok: bool
    action: str
    data: dict[str, Any]
    error: str = ""
    call_path: str = "native"
    bridge: str = "none"

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        out: dict[str, Any] = {
            "ok": self.ok,
            "action": self.action,
            "tool": self.action,
            "call_path": self.call_path,
            "bridge": self.bridge,
            "data": self.data,
        }
        if not self.ok:
            out["error"] = self.error
        return out


class ActionCatalogView(Protocol):

    def catalog(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]: ...


class SurfaceInvoker(Protocol):

PureHandler = Callable[[dict[str, Any]], ToolResult]

    "iris.session.get_state": "get_state",

}


def resolve_legacy_name(name: str) -> str:
    """Map deprecated iris.* seed ids to Control action names."""
    key = (name or "").strip()
    return _LEGACY_TO_ACTION.get(key, key)


def _domain_of(action: str) -> str:
    if action in ("ping", "get_catalog", "get_state"):
        return "session"
    if "." in action:
        return action.split(".", 1)[0]
    return "session"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SpeakAllowlist:
    """Single hand-maintained product list. Catalog/engine names derive from this."""

    grants: tuple[SpeakGrant, ...]

    def names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return tuple(sorted(g.action for g in self.grants))

    def grant(self, action: str) -> SpeakGrant | None:
        key = (action or "").strip()
        for g in self.grants:
            if g.action == key:
                return g
        return None

_BOUND_SURFACE: Any | None = None


def bind_live_control_surface(surface: Any | None) -> None:
    """Bind the GUI-owned surface so worker threads never enumerate Qt widgets."""
    global _BOUND_SURFACE
    _BOUND_SURFACE = surface


def engine_tool_schemas() -> tuple[dict[str, Any], ...]:
    """OpenAI function bodies for every engine-visible SpeakTool."""
    default_parameters = {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": True}
    return tuple(
        {
            "name": grant.action,
            "description": grant.summary or grant.action,
            "parameters": dict(grant.parameters or default_parameters),
        }
        for grant in PHASE4_ALLOWLIST.grants
    )


def _live_control_surface() -> Any | None:
    if _BOUND_SURFACE is not None:
        return _BOUND_SURFACE
    try:
        from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QApplication
    except ImportError:
        return None
    app = QApplication.instance()
    if app is None:
        return None
    for widget in app.topLevelWidgets():
        surface = getattr(widget, "_control_surface", None)
        if surface is not None:
            return surface
    return None


def _invoke_live_control(action: str, args: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """In-process Control invoke (no HTTP). None when Iris UI surface is absent."""
    surface = _live_control_surface()
    if surface is None:
        return None
    from iris.system.control_surface import call_registered

    return call_registered(surface, action, dict(args or {}), timeout=30.0)


class _LiveSurfaceInvoker:
    def invoke(self, action: str, args: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        return _invoke_live_control(action, args)


class _LiveActionCatalog:
    def spec(self, name: str) -> Any | None:
        surface = _live_control_surface()
        if surface is None:
            return None
        reg = getattr(surface, "registry", None)
        if reg is None:
            return None
        return reg.spec(name)

    def catalog(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        surface = _live_control_surface()
        if surface is None:
            return []
        reg = getattr(surface, "registry", None)
        if reg is None:
            return []
        return list(reg.catalog())

"""Per-turn tool error limits shared by the Iris sidecar."""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any


def _error_text(result: object) -> str:
    raw: object = result
    if isinstance(raw, str):
        text = raw.strip()
        if not text:
            return ""
        try:
            raw = json.loads(text)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            low = text.lower()
            return text if low.startswith(("error", "traceback")) else ""
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        return ""
    if raw.get("ok") is True and not raw.get("error"):
        return ""
    error = raw.get("error")
    if error:
        return " ".join(str(error).split())
    if raw.get("ok") is False:
        return "tool returned ok=false"
    return ""


def _target_key(name: str, args: object, error: str) -> str:
    try:
        payload = json.dumps(args or {}, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        payload = repr(args)
    digest = hashlib.sha256(payload.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")).hexdigest()
    return f"{name.strip()}:{digest}:{error}"


@dataclass
class ToolErrorBudget:
    """Stop after one identical target error 3 times or 10 total errors."""

    same_error_limit: int = 3
    total_error_limit: int = 10
    total_errors: int = 0
    repeated: Counter[str] = field(default_factory=Counter)
    reason: str = ""

    def observe(self, name: str, args: object, result: object) -> str:
        if self.reason:
            return self.reason
        error = _error_text(result)
        if not error:
            return ""
        self.total_errors += 1
        key = _target_key(name, args, error)
        self.repeated[key] += 1
        if self.repeated[key] >= self.same_error_limit:
            self.reason = (
                f"?숈씪 ??곸뿉??媛숈? ?꾧뎄 ?ㅻ쪟媛 {self.same_error_limit}??諛섎났?섏뼱 以묐떒?덉뒿?덈떎: "
                f"{name} ??{error[:240]}"
            )
        elif self.total_errors >= self.total_error_limit:
            self.reason = (
                f"???댁쓽 ?꾩껜 ?꾧뎄 ?ㅻ쪟媛 {self.total_error_limit}?뚯뿉 ?꾨떖?섏뿬 以묐떒?덉뒿?덈떎: "
                f"{name} ??{error[:240]}"
            )
        return self.reason


def _self_check() -> None:
    budget = ToolErrorBudget()
    failed = '{"ok": false, "error": "missing file"}'
    assert budget.observe("read_file", {"path": "a"}, failed) == ""
    assert budget.observe("read_file", {"path": "a"}, failed) == ""
    assert "3?? in budget.observe("read_file", {"path": "a"}, failed)

    total = ToolErrorBudget()
    for index in range(9):
        assert total.observe("tool", {"n": index}, failed) == ""
    assert "10?? in total.observe("tool", {"n": 9}, failed)
    assert ToolErrorBudget().observe("tool", {}, '{"ok": true}') == ""


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _self_check()
    print("tool error budget ok")

"""Central registry for all hermes-agent tools: each tool file calls ``registry.register()``
at import to declare schema, handler, toolset membership and availability check;
``model_tools.py`` queries the registry instead of keeping parallel data structures.
Cycle-safe import chain: this module imports nothing from model_tools or tool files;
tools/*.py import it at module level; model_tools.py imports both; run_agent/cli import
model_tools."""

import ast
import functools
import importlib
import inspect
import json
import logging
import sys
import threading
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from contextlib import contextmanager
from contextvars import ContextVar
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Set

from hermes_constants import hermes_home_key, normalize_scope

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_session_tool_scope = ContextVar("session_tool_scope", default=None)


@contextmanager
def session_tool_scope(scope):
    """Execution-owned overlay, additive to the existing profile registry."""
    token = _session_tool_scope.set(scope)
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        _session_tool_scope.reset(token)


def current_session_tool_scope():
    return _session_tool_scope.get()


def _session_slot_key():
    """The overlay slot key for the current session scope: writes go through ``normalize_scope``
    (``register``/``deregister``), so reads must key the same way or the overlay is invisible."""
    return normalize_scope(_session_tool_scope.get())


# Cap on a tool error body; only trims runaway interpolated exceptions (static msgs are ~115 chars).
_MAX_TOOL_ERROR_CHARS = 2048
_TOOL_ERROR_TRUNCATION_MARKER = "??[truncated]"
# Logs keep more of the body than the model sees, but still a bounded amount.
_MAX_LOGGED_ERROR_CHARS = 8192


def _bound_error_text(text: str) -> str:
    """Bound an error body destined for model context; logs keep a longer prefix."""
    if len(text) <= _MAX_TOOL_ERROR_CHARS:
        return text
    logger.debug(
        "tool error body truncated for context (%d chars): %s",
        len(text), text[:_MAX_LOGGED_ERROR_CHARS])
    return text[:_MAX_TOOL_ERROR_CHARS] + _TOOL_ERROR_TRUNCATION_MARKER


def _bound_json_error_result(result: str) -> str:
    """Trim an oversized ``error`` field in a JSON string result: handlers that
    ``json.dumps({"error": str(exc)})`` directly bypass ``tool_error``'s cap, so this runs
    at the dispatch boundary to stop unbounded errors stacking across retries."""
    if len(result) <= _MAX_TOOL_ERROR_CHARS or '"error"' not in result:
        return result
    try:
        payload = json.loads(result)
    except ValueError:
        return result
    error = payload.get("error") if isinstance(payload, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(error, str) or len(error) <= _MAX_TOOL_ERROR_CHARS:
        return result
    payload["error"] = _bound_error_text(error)
    return json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)


def _is_registry_register_call(node: ast.AST) -> bool:
    """True when *node* is a ``registry.register(...)`` call expression."""
    if not isinstance(node, ast.Expr) or not isinstance(node.value, ast.Call):
        return False
    func = node.value.func
    return (
        isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr == "register"
        and isinstance(func.value, ast.Name) and func.value.id == "registry")


def _module_registers_tools(module_path: Path) -> bool:
    """True when the module body (or a module-level ``for``) calls ``registry.register(...)``.
    Only module-body statements count, so helpers registering inside a function are skipped;
    a text prefilter avoids ``ast.parse`` for files lacking both words."""
    try:
        source = module_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
        if "registry" not in source or "register" not in source:
            return False
        tree = ast.parse(source, filename=str(module_path))
    except (OSError, SyntaxError):
        return False
    # Table-driven modules register several tools from one loop, still at import time.
    return any(
        _is_registry_register_call(stmt)
        or (isinstance(stmt, ast.For) and any(_is_registry_register_call(s) for s in stmt.body))
        for stmt in tree.body)


def _tool_module_candidates(tools_path: Path) -> list[Path]:
    """Flat ``tools/*.py`` modules plus the package entry point ``tools/<pkg>/tool.py``, in one
    sorted list. Only ``tool.py`` is scanned in a package, so every other file in it is a library
    by construction. Sorted after merging: ``register()`` lets a same-name, same-toolset duplicate
    overwrite silently, so the import order must not depend on file depth."""
    candidates = list(tools_path.glob("*.py")) + list(tools_path.glob("*/tool.py"))
    return sorted(candidates)


def discover_builtin_tools(tools_dir: Optional[Path] = None) -> list[str]:
    """Import built-in self-registering tool modules and return their module names. The
    per-file AST scan costs ~145 ms over ~100 files, so verdicts are memoized on disk keyed
    by ``(mtime_ns, size)``; a mismatch or corrupt cache re-scans that file. The write is
    best-effort and atomic, so concurrent processes race harmlessly."""
    from agent.safe_worker_policy import safe_worker_enabled
    if safe_worker_enabled():
        # Toolset filtering happens AFTER import. Keep the troubleshooting worker's
        # import graph closed over reviewed core tools, not plugin-backed wrappers
        # or a profile-writable discovery cache. Core approval/redaction stay intact.
        module_names = ["tools.file_tools", "tools.terminal_tool", "tools.process_registry"]
        for module_name in module_names:
            importlib.import_module(module_name)
        return module_names
    tools_path = (Path(tools_dir) if tools_dir is not None else Path(__file__).resolve().parent).resolve()
    cache = _load_discovery_cache()
    fresh_cache: dict[str, list] = {}
    cache_dirty = False
    module_names: list[str] = []
    for path in _tool_module_candidates(tools_path):
        if path.name in {"__init__.py", "registry.py", "mcp_tool.py"}:
            continue
        rel_parts = path.relative_to(tools_path).with_suffix("").parts
        if len(rel_parts) > 1 and not (path.parent / "__init__.py").exists():
            # setuptools' package finder drops a directory without __init__.py, so this tool would
            # register from a checkout and vanish from an installed wheel.
            logger.warning("Skipping %s: package %s has no __init__.py", path, path.parent.name)
            continue
        abs_path = str(path.resolve())
        try:
            st = path.stat()
            stat_key = (st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_size)
        except OSError:
            continue
        cached = cache.get(abs_path)
        if isinstance(cached, (list, tuple)) and len(cached) == 3 and tuple(cached[:2]) == stat_key:
            registers = bool(cached[2])
        else:
            registers = _module_registers_tools(path)
            cache_dirty = True
        fresh_cache[abs_path] = [stat_key[0], stat_key[1], registers]
        if registers:
            module_names.append(".".join(("tools", *rel_parts)))

    # Drop entries for files that no longer exist; rewrite only when changed.
    if cache_dirty or set(fresh_cache) != set(cache):
        _save_discovery_cache(fresh_cache)
    imported: list[str] = []
    for mod_name in module_names:
        try:
            importlib.import_module(mod_name)
            imported.append(mod_name)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning("Could not import tool module %s: %s", mod_name, e)
    return imported

    def _caller_module() -> str:
        """Best-effort module name of the registry method's caller (two frames up).
        ``deregister()`` takes only a tool name ??no handler for ``_plugin_owner_of`` ??        so frame inspection is the only way to know who is asking."""
        try:
            return sys._getframe(2).f_globals.get("__name__", "") or ""
        except Exception:
            return ""

    def register(
        self, name: str, toolset: str, schema: dict, handler: Callable,
        check_fn: Callable | None = None, requires_env: list | None = None, is_async: bool = False,
        description: str = "", emoji: str = "", max_result_size_chars: float | None = None,
        dynamic_schema_overrides: Callable | None = None, override: bool = False,
        scope: Optional[str] = None, execution_timeout: float | None = None):
        """Register a tool (called at import time by each tool file). ``override=True`` is an
        explicit opt-in for plugins replacing a built-in implementation (e.g. a headed-Chrome
        browser backend); without it, cross-toolset shadowing is rejected."""
        # Reject malformed schemas at registration, not at request time: a non-dict
        # ``parameters`` (e.g. a list) serializes into every provider request and 400s the
        # whole turn far from the offending plugin. Failing here names the culprit instead.
        if not isinstance(schema, dict):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Tool {name!r}: schema must be a dict, got {type(schema).__name__}")
        params = schema.get("parameters")
        if params is not None and not isinstance(params, dict):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Tool {name!r}: schema['parameters'] must be an object (JSON Schema dict), "
                f"got {type(params).__name__}")
        handler_owner = self._plugin_owner_of(handler)
        caller_owner = self._plugin_namespace_of_module(self._caller_module())
        owner = caller_owner or handler_owner
        if scope is None and owner is not None:
            scope = self._plugin_scope_of(owner)
        scope = normalize_scope(scope)
        with self._lock:
            target = self._slot(scope, create=True)
            existing = self._lookup(name, scope)
            plugin_override_denied = (
                owner is not None and not self._plugin_override_allowed(scope, owner))
            shadows_global = (
                owner is not None and scope is not None
                and name not in target and name in self._tools)
            if shadows_global:
                if not override:
                    logger.error(
                        "Tool registration REJECTED: plugin %r attempted to shadow global tool %r "
                        "without override=True", owner, name)
                    return
                if plugin_override_denied:
                    raise PermissionError(_OVERRIDE_DENIED_MSG.format(owner=owner, name=name))
            if existing and existing.toolset != toolset:
                if override:
                    if plugin_override_denied:
                        logger.error(
                            "Tool registration REJECTED: plugin %r attempted to override built-in "
                            "tool %r (existing toolset %r) without operator opt-in. Set "
                            "plugins.entries.<plugin_id>.allow_tool_override: true in config.yaml "
                            "to allow it.",
                            owner, name, existing.toolset)
                        raise PermissionError(_OVERRIDE_DENIED_MSG.format(owner=owner, name=name))
                    # Explicit opt-in (or non-plugin caller): INFO so the override is auditable.
                    logger.info(
                        "Tool '%s': toolset '%s' overriding existing toolset '%s' "
                        "(override=True opt-in)", name, toolset, existing.toolset)
                else:
                    # Reject every cross-toolset shadow (incl. MCP-to-MCP); same-toolset
                    # re-registration (MCP reconnect/refresh) stays allowed.
                    logger.error(
                        "Tool registration REJECTED: '%s' (toolset '%s') would shadow existing "
                        "tool from toolset '%s'. Pass override=True to register() if the "
                        "replacement is intentional, or deregister the existing tool first.",
                        name, toolset, existing.toolset)
                    return
            target[name] = ToolEntry(
                name=name, toolset=toolset, schema=schema, handler=handler, check_fn=check_fn,
                requires_env=requires_env or [], is_async=is_async,
                description=description or schema.get("description", ""), emoji=emoji,
                max_result_size_chars=max_result_size_chars, execution_timeout=execution_timeout,
                dynamic_schema_overrides=dynamic_schema_overrides)
            # Availability is derived per-tool (_toolset_has_exposable_tools), so this map no
            # longer gates a toolset; it still feeds get_toolset_requirements ->
            # TOOLSET_REQUIREMENTS["check_fn"], which banner.py reads (presence only,
            # never called) to classify an unavailable toolset as lazy-init vs disabled.
            if scope is None and check_fn and toolset not in self._toolset_checks:
                self._toolset_checks[toolset] = check_fn
            self._generation += 1

    def deregister(self, name: str, *, scope: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
        """Remove a tool; drops the toolset check/aliases if it was the last in its toolset.

        ``scope`` selects a profile overlay explicitly (multiplexed MCP tools live in the
        owning profile's overlay); plugin callers may not name another scope, non-plugin
        callers default to the process-global map. Gated by the same opt-in as
        ``register(override=True)``, else a plugin could deregister a tool it doesn't own
        and re-register over the empty slot (the override check only runs when an entry
        exists). ``mcp-*`` toolsets are exempt ??discovery repaves its own tools per refresh."""
        scope = normalize_scope(scope)
        with self._lock:
            caller_mod = self._caller_module()
            caller_owner = self._plugin_namespace_of_module(caller_mod)
            caller_scope = self._plugin_scope_of(caller_owner) if caller_owner is not None else None
            if caller_owner is not None and scope is not None and scope != caller_scope:
                raise PermissionError(
                    f"Plugin module {caller_mod!r} cannot deregister tools "
                    "outside its own profile scope.")
            if scope is None:
                scope = caller_scope
            target = self._slot(scope)
            entry = target.get(name)
            if entry is None:
                if scope is not None and caller_owner is not None and name in self._tools:
                    raise PermissionError(
                        f"Scoped plugin module {caller_mod!r} cannot deregister process-global "
                        f"tool {name!r}; register a scoped override instead.")
                return
            if not entry.toolset.startswith("mcp-"):
                owner = self._plugin_owner_of(entry.handler)
                # Ownership binds to the plugin package root (``hermes_plugins.{name}``), not

    def restore_registration(
        self, name: str, current: ToolEntry, previous: Optional[ToolEntry], *,
        scope: Optional[str] = None) -> bool:
        """Restore a host-owned registration if it is still current (plugin ownership ledger).
        The identity check is deliberate: another plugin (or ``PluginManager`` in a
        multi-profile process) may have registered a newer entry under the same name, and
        unloading this entry must leave that newer one untouched."""
        with self._lock:
            target = self._slot(scope, create=True)
            if target.get(name) is not current:
                return False
            if previous is None:
                target.pop(name, None)
            else:
                target[name] = previous
            if scope is not None and not target:
                self._scoped_tools.pop(scope, None)

            # Rebuild affected toolset checks from survivors: a plugin may have replaced an
            # entry in the same toolset, so its check_fn would otherwise linger after restore.
            affected_toolsets = {current.toolset}
            if previous is not None:
                affected_toolsets.add(previous.toolset)
            for toolset in affected_toolsets:
                surviving = self._toolset_entries(toolset, scope)
                check_fn = next((entry.check_fn for entry in surviving if entry.check_fn), None)

                    else:

                if not surviving and not any(e.toolset == toolset for e in in_overlays):

            self._generation += 1

    def dispatch(
        self, name: str, args: dict, *, scope: Optional[str] = None, **kwargs) -> str | dict:
        """Execute a tool handler by name: async handlers bridged via ``_run_async()``,
        results normalized, every exception returned as ``{"error": ...}``."""
        entry = self.get_entry(name, scope=scope)
        if not entry:
            return tool_error(f"Unknown tool: {name}")
        try:
            # Plugin contract (plugins/AGENTS.md): optional context kwargs (task_id, session_id, user_task,
            # parent_agent, ...) are signature-inspected like hook payloads, so a narrow ``handle(args)``
            # plugin handler is not broken by every field the dispatcher injects (#68318).
            kwargs = _kwargs_accepted_by(entry.handler, kwargs)
            if entry.is_async:
                from model_tools import _run_async
                result = _run_async(entry.handler(args, **kwargs))
            else:
                result = entry.handler(args, **kwargs)
            return self._normalize_handler_result(name, result)
        except Exception as e:
            # exc_info already renders the exception, so keep the message copy bounded.
            logger.exception("Tool %s dispatch error: %s", name, _bound_error_text(str(e)))
            # Sanitize so framing tokens/CDATA/fences in exception text aren't structural noise.
            raw = f"Tool execution failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
            try:
                from model_tools import _sanitize_tool_error
                sanitized = _sanitize_tool_error(raw)
            except Exception:
                sanitized = raw  # defensive: never let the sanitizer block error propagation
            return tool_error(sanitized)

class ChatRunMap:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._slots: dict[int, ChatRunSlot] = {}

    def slot(self, conversation_id: int) -> ChatRunSlot:
        cid = int(conversation_id)
        found = self._slots.get(cid)
        if found is None:
            found = ChatRunSlot(conversation_id=cid)
            self._slots[cid] = found
        return found

    def owning(self, turn_id: str) -> ChatRunSlot | None:
        if not turn_id:
            return None
        for item in self._slots.values():
            if item.gate.is_current(turn_id):
                return item
        return None

    def all_slots(self) -> list[ChatRunSlot]:
        return list(self._slots.values())

    def running_count(self) -> int:
        return sum(1 for item in self._slots.values() if item.gate.busy)

def _first_reply_title(
    messages: list[ChatMessage] | list[dict[str, str]],
) -> str:
    seen_user = False
    for msg in messages:
        role, content = _message_parts(msg)
        if role == "user" and _title_user_text(content):
            seen_user = True
            continue
        if not seen_user or role != "assistant":
            continue
        body = (content or "").replace(INTERRUPTED_NOTE, "\n").strip()
        if not body:

        title = summarize_reply(body)
        if title not in ("", DEFAULT_TITLE):
            return title
    return DEFAULT_TITLE

    return _first_reply_title(messages)

def _watch_trace(msg: str) -> None:
    line = f"pid={os.getpid()} {msg}\n"

    def _write() -> None:
        try:
            _WATCH_LOG.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with _WATCH_LOG.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                fh.write(line)
        except Exception:

    threading.Thread(target=_write, name="iris-side-watch", daemon=True).start()


def _write_terminal_file(payload: dict) -> None:
    """Pipe-independent done/fail so the host can land when stdout EINVAL."""
    kind = payload.get("t")
    if kind not in ("done", "fail"):
        return
    try:
        terminal_dir = _terminal_dir()
        terminal_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        line = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"
        path = terminal_dir / f"{os.getpid()}.ndjson"
        path.write_text(line, encoding="utf-8")
        _watch_trace(f"terminal_file {kind} path={path} dir={terminal_dir}")
    except Exception as exc:
        _watch_trace(f"terminal_file fail {exc!r}")


def _host_fds() -> list[int]:
    raw_fds: list[int] = []
    if _HOST_OUT_FD >= 0:
        raw_fds.append(_HOST_OUT_FD)
    try:
        raw_fds.append(int(_HOST_STDOUT.fileno()))
    except Exception:
        pass
    seen: set[int] = set()
    out: list[int] = []
    for fd in raw_fds:
        if fd < 0 or fd in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(fd)
        out.append(fd)
    return out


def _write_host_bytes(fd: int, data: bytes) -> None:
    """Non-blocking when possible so a full pipe cannot wedge done/fail forever."""
    try:
        os.set_blocking(fd, False)
    except (OSError, AttributeError, ValueError):
        pass
    offset = 0
    stall = 0
    while offset < len(data):
        try:
            written = os.write(fd, data[offset:])
        except BlockingIOError:
            stall += 1
            if stall > 50:
                raise OSError(22, "host stdout write would block")
            time.sleep(0.02)
            continue
        if written <= 0:
            raise OSError(22, "short write to host stdout")
        offset += written
        stall = 0


def _emit_terminal_via_udp(payload: dict) -> None:
    """done/fail over localhost UDP ??survives wedged stdout/stderr/file on Windows."""
    import socket

    port_raw = os.environ.get("IRIS_TERMINAL_UDP_PORT", "").strip()
    if not port_raw:
        raise OSError("IRIS_TERMINAL_UDP_PORT missing")
    port = int(port_raw)
    data = (json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    try:
        sock.sendto(data, ("127.0.0.1", port))
    finally:
        sock.close()
    _watch_trace(f"emit {payload.get('t')} udp ok bytes={len(data)} port={port}")


def _emit(payload: dict) -> None:
    # Defer callers off logging.Handler.emit.
    # done/fail: UDP (+ file backup). stdout/stderr terminal paths wedge the host.
    kind = payload.get("t")
    if kind in ("done", "fail"):
        blob = payload.get("text") or payload.get("detail") or ""
        _watch_trace(f"emit {kind} text_len={len(str(blob))}")
        # UDP only ??terminal files can freeze the Qt UI thread if polled there.
        try:
            _emit_terminal_via_udp(payload)
        except Exception as exc:
            _watch_trace(f"emit {kind} udp failed {exc!r}")
            _write_terminal_file(payload)
        return
    data = (json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
    last: OSError | None = None
    uniq_fds = _host_fds()
    for attempt in range(5):
        for fd in uniq_fds:
            try:
                with _EMIT_LOCK:
                    _write_host_bytes(fd, data)
                return
            except OSError as exc:
                last = exc
        time.sleep(0.02 * (attempt + 1))
    assert last is not None
    raise last

        """Boundary. Reject unknown roles and missing content."""
        if not isinstance(raw, list) or not raw:
            raise EngineError(EngineErrorCode.PROTOCOL, "transcript must be a non-empty list")
        parsed: list[ChatMessage] = []
        for row in raw:
            if not isinstance(row, dict):
                raise EngineError(EngineErrorCode.PROTOCOL, "each message must be a dict")
            try:
                role = Role(str(row.get("role", "")))
            except ValueError:
                raise EngineError(
                    EngineErrorCode.PROTOCOL,
                    f"unknown role: {row.get('role')!r}",
                ) from None
            content = _message_content(row)
            parsed.append(ChatMessage(role=role, content=content))
        return cls(messages=tuple(parsed))

    def split_for_agent(self) -> tuple[tuple[ChatMessage, ...], UserUtterance]:
        """Prior messages plus the trailing user utterance.

        Illegal when the last role is not USER.
        """
        if not self.messages or self.messages[-1].role is not Role.USER:
            raise EngineError(
                EngineErrorCode.NO_USER_UTTERANCE,
                "last message must be a user utterance",
            )
        return self.messages[:-1], UserUtterance(self.messages[-1].content)


def _message_content(row: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    model_content = row.get("model_content")
    if model_content:
        if not isinstance(model_content, str):
            raise EngineError(EngineErrorCode.PROTOCOL, "missing content")
        return model_content
    if "content" not in row or row["content"] is None:
        raise EngineError(EngineErrorCode.PROTOCOL, "missing content")
    content = row["content"]
    if not isinstance(content, str):
        raise EngineError(EngineErrorCode.PROTOCOL, "missing content")
    return content


class CancelToken:
    """Cross-thread cancel flag. The QThread owns the instance. The engine only reads."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._cancelled = False

    def cancel(self) -> None:
        self._cancelled = True

    def cancelled(self) -> bool:
        return self._cancelled

    EngineError,

    ToolProgress,
    TurnCancelled,
    TurnEvent,
    TurnFailed,
    TurnFinished,
)


def _text(raw: dict, key: str) -> str:
    value = raw.get(key, "")
    if value is None:
        return ""
    return str(value)


def _error_code(raw: object) -> EngineErrorCode:
    try:
        return EngineErrorCode(str(raw))
    except ValueError:
        return EngineErrorCode.UNKNOWN


def _protocol(detail: str) -> TurnFailed:
    return TurnFailed(EngineError(EngineErrorCode.PROTOCOL, detail))


def _parse_delta(raw: dict) -> TurnEvent:
    return ContentDelta(text=_text(raw, "text"))


def _parse_think(raw: dict) -> TurnEvent:
    return ReasoningDelta(text=_text(raw, "text"))


def _parse_tool(raw: dict) -> TurnEvent:
    return ToolProgress(label=_text(raw, "label"))


def _parse_app_ui(raw: dict) -> TurnEvent:
    return AppUiOfferEvent(
        title=_text(raw, "title") or "??,
        html_path=_text(raw, "html_path"),
        resource_uri=_text(raw, "resource_uri"),
    )


def _parse_done(raw: dict) -> TurnEvent:
    return TurnFinished(text=_text(raw, "text"))


def _parse_fail(raw: dict) -> TurnEvent:
    return TurnFailed(EngineError(_error_code(raw.get("code")), _text(raw, "detail")))


def _parse_cancel(_raw: dict) -> TurnEvent:
    return TurnCancelled()


_PARSERS: dict[str, Callable[[dict], TurnEvent]] = {
    "delta": _parse_delta,
    "think": _parse_think,
    "tool": _parse_tool,
    "tool_progress": _parse_tool,
    "app_ui": _parse_app_ui,
    "done": _parse_done,
    "fail": _parse_fail,
    "cancel": _parse_cancel,
}


def encode_host_command(kind: str, **fields: object) -> str:
    """One NDJSON line for the child stdin."""
    payload = {"t": kind, **fields}
    return json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"


def parse_turn_event(raw: dict) -> TurnEvent:
    """Sidecar stdout boundary. Unknown event names become TurnFailed(PROTOCOL)."""
    try:
        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
            return _protocol("event must be a dict")
        kind = raw.get("t")
        parser = _PARSERS.get(kind) if isinstance(kind, str) else None
        if parser is None:
            return _protocol(f"unknown event: {kind!r}")
        return parser(raw)
    except Exception as exc:
        return _protocol(str(exc))
